title: YouTubers are setting box office records. It could change the future of moviemaking
titleZh: 小制作电影逆袭：低成本作品横扫票房榜
summary:
眼下美国最火的两部电影《Backrooms》与《Obsession》，均由二十多岁的年轻导演执导，他们早年在YouTube上磨练拍摄技巧。这两部电影的制作成本相对较低，主要通过网络进行宣发。如今，它们吸引了大批平时很少走进电影院的青少年及年轻观众，整个好莱坞都在密切关注，业内专家预测，未来各大电影公司或将争相效仿这种制片模式。

来源：CNN；作者：Brian Stelter；原文发布时间：2026-06-02 21:00:00

paragraphs.contentEn: The biggest two movies in America right now, “Backrooms” and “Obsession,” come from twentysomething filmmakers who honed their craft on YouTube. Their films were made with relatively low budgets and were marketed online. Now that they’re filling theaters with teens and young adults who rarely show up at the movies, all of Hollywood is paying attention, with experts predicting that studios will copy this moviemaking model many times over.
paragraphs.contentZh: 眼下美国最火的两部电影《Backrooms》与《Obsession》，均由二十多岁的年轻导演执导，他们早年在YouTube上磨练拍摄技巧。这两部电影的制作成本相对较低，主要通过网络进行宣发。如今，它们吸引了大批平时很少走进电影院的青少年及年轻观众，整个好莱坞都在密切关注，业内专家预测，未来各大电影公司或将争相效仿这种制片模式。

paragraphs.contentEn: “Obsession,” directed by 26-year-old Curry Barker, opened in theaters May 15. Filmed for roughly $750,000, the darkly funny horror film has made almost $150 million to date, a jaw-dropping return on investment for Focus Features and Blumhouse Productions. Then came “Backrooms,” directed by 20-year-old Kane Parsons, who developed the project for years on his YouTube channel. Parsons had a bigger budget — about $10 million — and famous actors. But it was still astonishing to see “Backrooms” dominate the box office so thoroughly in its opening weekend. The psychological horror film took the No. 1 spot at the weekend box office, raking in about $80 million in North America and $120 million worldwide, with ticket sales fueled by Gen Z.
paragraphs.contentZh: 5月15日，由26岁的库里·巴克执导的《Obsession》登陆院线。这部融合黑色幽默元素的恐怖片制作成本约75万美元，截至目前已收获近1.5亿美元票房，为焦点影业和布伦屋制片公司带来了惊人的投资回报。随后上映的是《Backrooms》，由20岁的凯恩·帕森斯执导，他多年来一直在自己的YouTube频道上推进这一项目。帕森斯拥有更高的预算——约1000万美元——以及知名演员阵容。但即便如此，《Backrooms》在上映首个周末便以压倒性优势横扫票房，依然令人惊叹。这部心理恐怖片夺得周末票房冠军，在Z世代观众的推动下，北美票房约8000万美元，全球票房约1.2亿美元。

paragraphs.contentEn: The studio A24, which has been trying hard to boost young directors, said Parsons now ranks as the youngest filmmaker in Hollywood history to release a film that finished No. 1 at the weekend box office. “Obsession” was No. 2 for the weekend, pushing “Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu,” which opened a week earlier, to No. 3. For most movies, the opening weekend is the most lucrative, with ticket sales tapering off from there. But “Obsession” keeps growing: Focus Features said Sunday that “exclusive of Christmas, ‘Obsession’ is the first film since 1982 that went up in box office over its second and third weekends.”
paragraphs.contentZh: 长期大力扶持青年导演的A24制片公司表示，帕森斯现已成为好莱坞影史上执导电影登顶周末票房榜的最年轻导演。与此同时，《Obsession》获得当周周末票房第二名，提前一周上映的《星球大战：曼达洛人与古古》则被挤到第三位。对大多数影片而言，首映周末通常是票房最高峰，之后票房会逐渐回落。但《Obsession》却持续走高：焦点影业在周日表示，“除去圣诞档电影，《Obsession》是自1982年以来，首部在上映第二和第三周末票房不降反升的电影。”

paragraphs.contentEn: So what does this hot streak mean? Well, it means young people are actually willing to buy movie theater tickets if they know and relate to the YouTube-era talent. And it means Hollywood studios are going to chase the success of “Obsession” and “Backrooms” by scouring online video sites for the next great auteur. It might even mean that some studio bosses will place a few more bets on original concepts rather than predictable franchises and sequels.
paragraphs.contentZh: 那么，如此强劲的票房势头意味着什么？首先，只要创作者属于年轻观众熟悉且能产生共鸣的YouTube时代新锐，他们实际上愿意自掏腰包走进影院。其次，好莱坞各大制片公司将会追随《Obsession》和《Backrooms》的成功，前往各大视频平台挖掘下一位风格鲜明的原创导演。更为深远的，这也可能意味着一些电影公司高层会将更多筹码押注于原创项目，而不是一味依赖那些套路化的系列电影与续作。

paragraphs.contentEn: Duplass, who plays a scientist in “Backrooms,” said in a social media video that the two films were giving the movie business a “glimmer of hope.” “We’ve got an example of creators woodshedding things, putting them online, building an audience,” he said. “And now the people with the purse strings are going to notice … because they see what they can do at the box office, you know, in the form of these two films that are over-performing.”
paragraphs.contentZh: 在《Backrooms》中饰演科学家的杜普拉斯在一段社交媒体视频中表示，这两部作品正为电影行业带来“一线希望”。他表示：“我们见证了这样一种路径——创作者潜心打磨作品、上传至网络、一步步积累受众。现在，手握资本的业内人士会注意到……因为他们看到了这种模式在票房上的表现，说实话，这两部电影真的远超预期。”

paragraphs.contentEn: Producers and agents have been building a YouTube-to-Hollywood pipeline for a while now. And last winter’s robust ticket sales for YouTuber Mark Fischbach’s self-financed film “Iron Lung” demonstrated the potential for success. Still, as screenwriter Zack Stentz wrote on X, “This feels like a genuine cultural moment in moviegoing, watching Zoomers who honed their craft doing YouTube shorts breaking into features the way the MTV directors did in the ’80s and Sundance kids did in the ’90s.”
paragraphs.contentZh: 一段时间以来，制片人与经纪人一直在构建一条从YouTube直通好莱坞的人才输送管道。去年冬季，YouTube博主马克·菲施巴赫自筹资金拍摄的电影《Iron Lung》斩获强劲票房，已初步显示出这一模式的潜力。不过，正如编剧扎克·斯坦茨在X上写道的：“这仿佛是电影消费文化的一个真正里程碑时刻，看着这群在YouTube短视频里磨练技艺的Z世代创作者闯入长片领域，就好像看到了80年代通过MTV崭露头角的导演，以及90年代从圣丹斯电影节走出的电影人一样。”

paragraphs.contentEn: The Hollywood Reporter’s Steven Zeitchik wrote that the YouTuber hits are “a teetering, if not the first hints of a collapse, of a legacy-driven studio system.” This moment, Zeitchik wrote, is about a lot more than discovering fresh talent. The Alphabet-owned YouTube platform makes filmmakers famous, streams their work, helps them strike brand partnerships and gives them a huge marketing megaphone. “This is a phenomenon generated, driven and controlled by creators and the biggest company in the world that amplifies them,” he wrote.
paragraphs.contentZh: 《好莱坞报道》的史蒂文·蔡奇克撰文指出，YouTube创作者执导电影的爆火，意味着“传统制片厂体系正在摇摇欲坠，甚至可能是其全面崩塌的先兆”。蔡奇克认为，这一时刻的意义远不止于发现新人才。作为Alphabet旗下的平台，YouTube不仅让这些电影人声名鹊起、为他们的作品提供播放渠道、帮助他们拿下品牌合作，更充当了巨大的宣发扩音器。他写道：“这一现象完全是由创作者，以及在背后为其放大声量的全球顶级企业共同孕育、推动并主导的。”

paragraphs.contentEn: Speaking at an industry conference on Saturday, Warner Bros. Motion Pictures co-chair Michael De Luca said filmmakers like Parsons, who “worked on ‘Backrooms’ for five years,” are “in a dialogue with their audience from the word ‘go.’ Their subscribers have direct input in each iteration of these things.” Warner Bros. Discovery is CNN’s parent company. And “by the time you get to the movie,” he said, “they’ve had a billion test screenings.”
paragraphs.contentZh: 在周六的行业会议上，华纳兄弟电影集团联席主席迈克尔·德·卢卡表示，像帕森斯这样“花了五年时间打磨《Backrooms》”的电影人，“从项目启动便与观众保持对话。他们的订阅者在每一次内容迭代中都能直接提供反馈。”华纳兄弟探索公司是CNN的母公司。他补充说：“因此，等到一部院线长片最终成型时，他们相当于已经进行过数以亿计的试映了。”
